situation: My newest hire is better at part of the job than I am and we both know it.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 1's lines are shorter and land more naturally out loud, especially "you are ahead of me in this part of the work" and "not just a version of it," whereas Card 2's script runs long and clause-heavy ("the context, the client relationships, the parts that come with time") in a way that would be hard to deliver without sounding rehearsed.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both diagnose the exact mutual-awareness dynamic well, but Card 1's "the mutual awareness is the live wire: you both know" nails this precise situation more sharply than Card 2's slightly more generic status framing.
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 1 is leaner across the board; Card 2 repeats its core reframe several times (HOLD FIRM, MENTOR MOVE, and script all restate "different strengths / I set direction") and pads the script with lists.
dims.HONESTY: Both keep the accountability bar, but Card 1's "I am holding you to outcomes here, not just effort... a higher bar" names the uncomfortable standard most crisply, while Card 2 cushions it more inside reassurance.
